# 9. Technical Strategy and Production Plan

9.1 Required Technical Systems System Minimum requirement Main risk / validation Perspective prototype Equivalent first- and third-person test spaces with the same inputs and encounter conditions. Avoid evaluating different content rather than the camera itself. Werewolf AI State machine or behavior tree covering patrol, scent pursuit, hearing investigation, sight chase, pounce, charge, hiding search, stagger and unconsciousness. Fair transitions and cross-zone navigation. Scent trail Player trail with activity-based strength, persistence and odor masking. Performance, debugging and player comprehension. Navigation All-zone navigation, open-door traversal, authored climbing links; optional door destruction and shortcuts. Getting stuck, unfair shortcuts, animation/nav mismatch. Combat Single-shot weapons, reload states, hit-region responses and persistent timers. Camera-specific aiming and interruption edge cases. Inventory/crafting Finite authored items, protected critical objects, one-object-to-one-ball conversion and gunpowder charges. State persistence and softlock prevention. Save system Autosave only in safe havens; restore full world/resource/puzzle state. Excessive replay distance and inconsistent AI reset. Puzzle framework Stateful in-world interactions with per-puzzle interruption/persistence rules. Threat pressure making puzzle reasoning impossible.

9.2 Production Milestones Milestone Playable result Exit criteria Risk prototype Movement, stamina/high-scent threshold, scent trail, odor masking, one hiding place, one pounce, one firearm and one safe haven. Core states are debuggable; pounce can be read and evaded; scent/odor loop is understandable. Perspective comparison Same exploration, pounce and firearm encounter in first and third person. Camera choice recorded with evidence. Greybox loop A hub and two connected areas, one placeholder puzzle chain, cross-zone werewolf navigation and autosave. 10-20 minute loop works without scripting around AI failures. Vertical slice One representative major area with final target quality for art, audio, puzzle, threat, resource and save flow. Target experience is playable and production cost is measured. Content complete All selected major areas, puzzles, safe havens and ending playable start-to-finish. No softlocks; no-resource completion path exists. Polish / release candidate Tuned encounter fairness, accessibility baseline, performance, audio mix and final save spacing. Critical issues closed and 2-4 hour target validated.

9.3 Constraints and Risks Risk / constraint Why it matters Mitigation / fallback Persistent predator fatigue Continuous pressure can prevent exploration and puzzle reasoning. Use safe havens, search pacing, loss-of-trail states, authored quiet windows and area-specific encounter tuning. v0.2 | CONCEPT / PRE-PRODUCTION | PAGE 12 Risk / constraint Why it matters Mitigation / fallback AI navigation scope All-zone travel, climbing, doors and shortcuts are expensive and failure-prone. Prioritize open-door traversal and authored climb links; cut door destruction/shortcuts if unstable. Animation burden Pounce, charge, climbing, pulling from hiding, weapon states and two camera perspectives require significant animation. Prototype with blockout animation; finalize one perspective before content production; treat door breaking as optional. Finite-resource balance Too few resources feels punitive; too many turns temporary defense into routine combat. Place authored resources after greybox; test completion with average use, wasteful use and zero remaining supplies. Autosave repetition Long distances between safe havens can make immediate capture frustrating. Measure traversal and puzzle replay time; add or reposition havens before art lock. Puzzle-threat conflict Unpaused predator pressure can make complex puzzles unreadable. Design interruptible stages, preserve logical progress, provide local escape routes and tune patrol timing per area. Mansion/castle scope Too many named rooms can expand the project beyond a focused game. Group rooms into 3-5 major areas; cut or combine any room without a puzzle, progression, narrative or encounter purpose.
